note.question: Can a simple token rule make anonymous self-interested computing servers share idle capacity as efficiently as a fully informed central dispatcher?
note.overview: N self-interested servers with private queue and token states repeatedly decide whether to process own jobs, help others, waste capacity, or request help. The mechanism induces an incomplete-information stochastic dynamic game analyzed through fluid mean-field equilibrium and approximate-best-response guarantees.

components.label: Model sequence and system structure
components.explanation: Jobs and service-capacity units arrive independently to every server in continuous time. At any time, a server may spend tokens to request help for one or more queued jobs and move them irrevocably to the shared pool. On a capacity arrival, it may serve a local job, offer help to the pool, or idle; offering help earns a token with probability φ. The process repeats indefinitely and each server minimizes long-run average cost.
